text:
Marathon Petroleum dropped 7.4% today after oil prices fell sharply on renewed diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions in the Middle East. Iran's supreme leader and top security officials discussed conditions to end the U.S.-Israeli conflict, and Saudi Arabia's defense minister met with Iran's president in Tehran—both moves signaled reduced geopolitical risk and sent crude prices lower. For a refiner, lower oil costs are a double-edged sword: while it cuts input costs, it also compresses the profit margin they earn on each gallon processed (the difference between what they pay for crude and what they collect for refined products).

The stock has already fallen 8.6% over two weeks as geopolitical tensions have eased from their peak earlier in the month. Even though refineries are running at a healthy 93.4% capacity and product inventories remain moderate, investors appear to be pricing in a weaker environment for refining margins as crude becomes less scarce and the premium paid for supply certainty evaporates.
